title: hotfix: slo-enforcer backoff and regional failover stabilization
author: Maya Chen
description: Summary: urgent hotfix to stabilize SLO enforcement after a production regression where aggressive load-shedding and regional failovers were triggered by an edge-case in the rolling-window aggregation logic. This PR corrects the aggregation, adds a cooldown/backoff timer to the enforcer, improves tracing/metrics to make incidents diagnosable, and includes a focused test suite to prevent regressions. Motivation: on 2026-02-14 we observed cascading regional failovers for a small subset of customers after a spike in short-lived requests. Root cause: the enforcer aggregated hotspot counts using an incorrect timestamp bucket offset which double-counted transient bursts, causing the circuit-breaker to trip prematurely. Changes: - Fix rolling-window aggregation to use monotonic windowing and correct bucket alignment. - Add a cooldown/backoff state/TTL for regional failover decisions to avoid thrashing during transient spikes. - Surface additional metrics and traces: slo_enforcer.window_count, slo_enforcer.cooldown_state, slo_enforcer.backoff_multiplier. - Improve unit/integration tests to simulate rapid burst patterns and verify non-thrashing behavior. - Deployment: include a controlled k8s manifest patch to allow fast rollback. Rollout plan: squash-merge to main, staged rollout to canary region for 10m, monitor slo_enforcer.cooldown_state and request success rate, then promote globally if stable. Checklist: - [x] Reproduce locally with synthetic burst workload - [x] Unit+integration tests added - [x] Metrics/traces instrumented - [x] Runbook updated with rollback steps - [x] Verified canary in staging Notes: this is intentionally conservative (cooldown defaults to 30s, backoff multiplier capped at 4) to favor availability over strict SLO enforcement while we validate telemetry. Related: ENG-4721 (incident), SUP-9812 (customer report).
